name: isolate_child
prose: void process::isolate_child(const optional<passwd::user>& unprivileged_user, const fs::path& work_directory). Precondition: work_directory names an existing directory that the process can chdir into; when unprivileged_user is set and the real uid is 0, the user's uid and gid are valid. Postcondition: in this order it (1) calls isolate_path, which, only if unprivileged_user is set and the current user (passwd::current_user(), based on the real uid) is root, chowns work_directory to the unprivileged user's uid/gid for whichever of the two differs from the process's current uid/gid (no chown if both already match); (2) chdirs into work_directory; (3) calls utils::unlimit_core_size(), a best-effort raise of the soft RLIMIT_CORE to the hard limit whose result is ignored; (4) calls signals::reset_all(), and only logs a warning if that fails (so default signal dispositions are not guaranteed); (5) prepare_environment: unsets LANG and LC_ALL/COLLATE/CTYPE/MESSAGES/MONETARY/NUMERIC/TIME and sets HOME and TMPDIR to work_directory and TZ to UTC; (6) sets umask 0022; (7) if unprivileged_user is set and the current user is root: if the user's gid differs from getgid() it calls setgid, and then, only if getuid() is 0, setgroups(1, [gid]); if the user's uid differs from getuid() it calls setuid. If no unprivileged user is given, or the process is not root, no uid/gid/group changes are made. A failure of chown, chdir, setgid, setgroups or setuid prints a message with strerror to stderr and ends the process with std::exit(124) (process::exit_isolation_failure); exceptions from passwd::current_user, from environment functions or from the logging code are not caught and propagate. Otherwise returns nothing.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): setgid and setgroups happen only when the target gid differs from getgid() (lines 154-165); also corrected: core limit is raised best effort, not 'removed', and unlimit_core_size does not throw

name: ldns_dnssec_zone_sign_flg
prose: ldns_status ldns_dnssec_zone_sign_flg(ldns_dnssec_zone *zone, ldns_rr_list *new_rrs, ldns_key_list *key_list, int (*func)(ldns_rr *, void *), void *arg, int flags) (dnssec_sign.c lines 1374-1442). Precondition: the zone is already sorted; if LDNS_SIGN_WITH_ZONEMD is set in flags, zone->soa must be non-NULL; if zone->names is non-NULL its root node's data must be valid. Postcondition: returns LDNS_STATUS_ERR if zone, new_rrs or key_list is NULL (nothing else done). Otherwise: if flags has LDNS_SIGN_WITH_ZONEMD and zone->soa->rrsets has no ZONEMD rrset, it links a temporary ZONEMD rrset placeholder (a local variable) into the sorted rrsets list. It then calls ldns_dnssec_zone_mark_glue and returns its status at once if not OK; then, unless LDNS_SIGN_NO_KEYS_NO_NSECS is set with an empty key list, if zone->names exists and the first name has no NSEC it calls ldns_dnssec_zone_create_nsecs and returns its status at once if not OK. On either of these two early error returns the placeholder, if it was inserted, is NOT removed and stays linked in zone->soa->rrsets although it is a dead local variable. Otherwise it calls ldns_dnssec_zone_create_rrsigs_flg and keeps its status in result, removes the placeholder if one was inserted, and returns dnssec_zone_equip_zonemd(zone, new_rrs, key_list, flags) when LDNS_SIGN_WITH_ZONEMD is set (in which case the create_rrsigs_flg status in result is discarded and a failure to sign is not reported by this function), or result otherwise.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): with ZONEMD the rrsig status is ignored (lines 1423-1441); verified early-return placeholder leak (1406-1421)

name: ldns_dnssec_zone_mark_and_get_glue
prose: ldns_status ldns_dnssec_zone_mark_and_get_glue(ldns_dnssec_zone *zone, ldns_rr_list *glue_list) (dnssec_sign.c lines 675-752). Precondition: glue_list may be NULL; every name's data in zone->names is a valid ldns_dnssec_name. Postcondition: returns LDNS_STATUS_NULL if zone or zone->names is NULL (nothing changed). Otherwise it walks the names in tree order, tracking a current zone cut. A name strictly below the current cut (ldns_dname_is_subdomain) that has no SOA rrset is marked is_glue = true (is_glue is only ever set here, never cleared) and, if the cut is a delegation (NS without SOA) and glue_list is non-NULL, every RR of its A and AAAA rrsets is pushed onto glue_list; names below a DNAME cut are marked but their addresses are not collected. A name that is not below the cut (or has a SOA) ends the current cut and is then examined as a possible new cut: a name with an NS rrset and no SOA becomes a delegation cut (the cut name itself is not marked is_glue, but if glue_list is non-NULL its own A/AAAA records are pushed), and otherwise a name with a DNAME rrset becomes a DNAME cut. If pushing onto glue_list fails the function returns LDNS_STATUS_MEM_ERR at once, leaving the walk unfinished (marks made so far stay). Returns LDNS_STATUS_OK after the whole walk.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): code returns LDNS_STATUS_NULL for NULL zone/names so 'non-NULL' is not a precondition; R1 claims already covered

name: main
prose: int main(int argc, char *argv[]) of the drill DNS client (ldns drill.c lines 107-1057; read in full, callees not read). The result variable starts at 0. Control flow: it duplicates argv[0], parses options with getopt and then the non-option arguments (@server, +nsid, a name, type, class), builds the query name (reverse names for -x), creates a resolver (from resolv.conf or from the @server argument), applies the resolver options and optional TSIG settings, and switches on the purpose (trace, secure trace, chase, answer-from-file, query-to-file, or a normal query / query file / AXFR). Paths that reach the 'exit' label (which frees qname, source address, resolvers, key list, command-line rr list, trace start name, progname and TSIG strings, runs OpenSSL cleanups if configured, and returns result): -v and -h (result EXIT_SUCCESS), unknown options (EXIT_FAILURE), -y when built without SSL (EXIT_FAILURE), an unparsable -d name (EXIT_FAILURE), a failed WSAStartup under Windows (EXIT_FAILURE), a failed resolver creation (EXIT_FAILURE), no name with no -i and no query file (usage, EXIT_FAILURE), an AXFR whose first record cannot be read (message printed, result left at 0), the end of an AXFR transfer (result 0), and the normal end of each switch case. In the normal query case result is EXIT_FAILURE if no packet was received; with -k keys under HAVE_SSL it is the status from ldns_pkt_verify (or from ldns_verify_denial when verification returns LDNS_STATUS_ERR), and the packet is freed afterwards, except that a query of type ANY with keys given leaves the switch before dumping to the answer file and before freeing the packet. In secure-trace mode result is the status of do_secure_trace; in chase mode result is EXIT_FAILURE when no packet is returned, otherwise the value from do_chase (0 on LDNS_STATUS_OK, else the status code) when an answer exists. Many other failures call exit() or the error() helper (which prints and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE)) directly and skip the cleanup label: conflicting -T/-S, a non-numeric -V, root-hints errors, -b/-p conversion errors, unparsable -k files, a missing server name after '@', EDNS option errors, bad reverse-lookup addresses, a bad -I address, errors resolving or adding the nameserver, failure to build the query name, errors preparing or sending a query (including a failed AXFR start, which calls error()), a send error with a query file, and a secure trace without SSL support.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R15 (AXFR no-first-record jumps to exit with result still 0) and R17 (a failed ldns_axfr_start calls error(), which exits, not goto exit; error() in drill/error.c:42-49 ends with exit(EXIT_FAILURE)); old prose wrongly grouped failed AXFR start with the cleanup paths. Read the whole function

name: ldns_rr2buffer_str_fmt
prose: ldns_status ldns_rr2buffer_str_fmt(ldns_buffer *output, const ldns_output_format *fmt, const ldns_rr *rr) (host2str.c lines 1850-2072). Precondition: output is a valid buffer; fmt may be NULL (then ldns_output_format_default is used); rr must be non-NULL unless the format does not have LDNS_FMT_SHORT; when the NSEC3-chain comment flag and a hashmap are in use, the hashmap must contain the looked-up names (ldns_rbtree_search results are dereferenced without a NULL check). Postcondition: without LDNS_FMT_SHORT and with a NULL rr it appends '; (null)\n' only if LDNS_COMMENT_NULLS is set and returns the buffer's status. Otherwise it appends the owner name (error status from the dname conversion is returned at once), a tab and the TTL unless the RR is a question, a tab, the class (class conversion errors returned at once), a tab; if the output format covers the RR type it appends the RFC 3597 form via ldns_rr2buffer_str_rfc3597 (which itself ends with a newline) and returns that function's result immediately; otherwise it appends the type (errors returned at once), then a tab if there is rdata, or '\# 0' for an empty non-question RR. With LDNS_FMT_SHORT only the rdata part is printed (or '# 0' when there is none). It then prints each rdata field separated by single spaces (RRSIG inception, expiration and signature replaced by '(null)' with LDNS_FMT_ZEROIZE_RRSIGS, the SOA serial printed with %10lu with LDNS_FMT_PAD_SOA_SERIAL, other fields via ldns_rdf2buffer_str_fmt); a non-OK status from a field is returned at once. If there is rdata it then appends the per-type comments selected by the flags (DNSKEY key id/type/size, RRSIG key id, DS bubblebabble, NSEC3 flags and chain names). Finally it appends a newline in the normal path and returns ldns_buffer_status(output); that final status, not a constant LDNS_STATUS_OK, is what a successful call returns, so a failure of an earlier printf to the buffer (for example running out of space) is reported at the end or at the next status check.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): normal path does append a trailing newline (line 2070); reviewer R1 (non-OK from printf paths) RIGHT and included

name: ldns_send_buffer
prose: ldns_status ldns_send_buffer(ldns_pkt **result, ldns_resolver *r, ldns_buffer *qb, ldns_rdf *tsig_mac) (net.c lines 545-766). Precondition: r is non-NULL (asserted), qb holds a query packet; result and tsig_mac may be NULL. Postcondition: returns LDNS_STATUS_QDCOUNT_MUST_BE_ONE, leaving *result untouched, if qb has fewer than 6 bytes or its QDCOUNT is not 1. It then optionally randomises the nameserver order (resolver random flag) and tries each nameserver in turn, skipping those whose rtt is LDNS_RESOLV_RTT_INF and those excluded by the resolver's IP-family restriction; for each tried server it sends over TCP (usevc) or UDP up to 'retry' times, marking the server's rtt as INF and recording the status when sending fails, and discarding a reply whose transaction id does not match (status LDNS_STATUS_ID_DID_NOT_MATCH). With no usable reply and the resolver fail flag set it frees its buffers and returns the recorded status (or LDNS_STATUS_ERR if that is 0) without touching *result; without the fail flag it moves on to the next server. If a reply arrives and ldns_wire2pkt fails, it frees its temporaries and returns that error, *result untouched. The first successfully parsed reply stops the loop and overwrites status with LDNS_STATUS_OK, so earlier send or id errors are not reported when a later server answers. If every server was skipped (or there are none) it returns LDNS_STATUS_RES_NO_NS with *result untouched. After the loop, with HAVE_SSL, a non-NULL tsig_mac and a reply, a failed TSIG verification sets status LDNS_STATUS_CRYPTO_TSIG_BOGUS (the reply is kept). If a reply exists and its QDCOUNT is not 1 the status becomes LDNS_STATUS_QDCOUNT_MUST_BE_ONE and the reply is freed; or if the query cannot be re-parsed, has QDCOUNT other than 1, or its question differs from the reply's, the status becomes LDNS_STATUS_QUERY_DID_NOT_MATCH and the reply is freed (these statuses overwrite a TSIG status). Finally, if result is non-NULL, *result is set to the reply or to NULL when none was obtained or it was rejected, and the status is returned: LDNS_STATUS_OK for a good reply, the TSIG, QDCOUNT or QUERY_DID_NOT_MATCH status as above, or the last send/id error when no reply was obtained from any server. If result is NULL a good reply is not stored and is not freed.
note: reviewer R1 RIGHT (TSIG failure keeps the reply in *result); reviewer R15 WRONG: status is overwritten by LDNS_STATUS_OK at line 686 when ldns_wire2pkt succeeds, so earlier send/ID errors are not returned when a later reply is stored

name: ldns_resolver_nameservers_randomize
prose: void ldns_resolver_nameservers_randomize(ldns_resolver *r) (resolver.c lines 1546-1568; the slice shows only the body). Precondition: r is non-NULL (asserted when assertions are enabled), and its nameserver array and rtt array each hold at least ldns_resolver_nameserver_count(r) entries; ldns_get_random() is available. Postcondition: for each index i from 0 up to the nameserver count it picks j = ldns_get_random() % count and swaps ns[i] with ns[j] and rtt[i] with rtt[j] (so each nameserver keeps its own rtt), which permutes both arrays in place; it then stores the same ns array pointer back with ldns_resolver_set_nameservers. It does not check the resolver's random flag, allocates and frees nothing, and returns nothing. If the count is 0 the loop does not run. The loop indices i and j are uint16_t.

name: ldns_rr_new_frm_str_internal
prose: static ldns_status ldns_rr_new_frm_str_internal(ldns_rr **newrr, const char *str, uint32_t default_ttl, const ldns_rdf *origin, ldns_rdf **prev, bool question, bool *explicit_ttl) (rr.c lines 119-668; ldns_rr_new_frm_str is a wrapper at line 670 that passes question = false and explicit_ttl = NULL). Precondition: str is a NUL-terminated presentation-format RR; newrr, origin, prev and explicit_ttl may each be NULL; *prev, if prev and *prev are non-NULL, is an owner rdf that the function may free and replace. Postcondition: it allocates a new RR and temporary buffers, splits str into owner, TTL, class, type and rdata tokens and parses them. On success it returns LDNS_STATUS_OK and stores the new RR in *newrr (caller owns it), or frees it if newrr is NULL. Non-OK returns: LDNS_STATUS_MEM_ERR on allocation failures (including a failed clone of the owner for '@' or for an empty owner), SYNTAX_ERR (owner token or owner name unparsable, or appending the origin fails), SYNTAX_TTL_ERR, SYNTAX_CLASS_ERR, SYNTAX_TYPE_ERR, SYNTAX_RDATA_ERR (bad rdata token, bad \# data, or a field that cannot be converted), the status of ldns_wire2rdf or of ldns_dname_cat for a name rdata, LDNS_STATUS_SYNTAX_SUPERFLUOUS_TEXT_ERR if rdata text remains after the fields are parsed, and LDNS_STATUS_SYNTAX_MISSING_VALUE_ERR when a non-question RR of a known type (not in \# format) has fewer rdata fields than the type's minimum. On these failures the buffers and the partial RR are freed and *newrr is not set. Exception: when the owner is not '@' and not empty, prev is non-NULL and cloning the new owner for *prev fails (lines 325-330), the code jumps to the error label without setting a status, so it returns LDNS_STATUS_OK (the initial status) with no RR stored. Other details: if the second token does not start with a digit it is taken as the class (or as the type when it is not a class), the TTL is default_ttl (or LDNS_DEFAULT_TTL if that is 0) and *explicit_ttl is set false, otherwise it is true; an unknown type name yields type 0 without error; *prev may already have been freed and replaced with the new owner when a later failure occurs.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R17): clone failure of *prev in the non-@ branch does 'goto error' without setting MEM_ERR (status stays LDNS_STATUS_OK); slice cut head; real function is the static _internal one

name: ch_get
prose: static int ch_get(void) (less ch.c lines 147-376). Reads the module's global file state. Postcondition: returns the byte (as an unsigned char value 0..255) at the current read position (ch_block, ch_offset) of the current file, or EOI (-1), or '?' (63). Returns EOI at once if thisfile is NULL. If the head buffer holds the wanted block and offset, returns that byte. Otherwise it clears waiting_for_data and looks the block up in the hash chain; if found with data at the offset it moves the buffer to the head of the LRU and hash chains and returns the byte. Then, if ABORT_SIGS() (interrupt, window-change interrupt or stop in sigs) is set it returns EOI. If the block is in no buffer it may allocate a new buffer via ch_addbuf (setting autobuf off if that fails) and reuses the least recently used buffer for the block. In the read loop it returns EOI if the position is at or past the known length of a seekable or help file (after re-checking the size with ch_resize); for a pipe at that point it tries one more read (read_pipe_at_eof). If the file position differs from the wanted position it returns '?' when the input cannot seek, or shows 'seek error' and returns EOI if lseek fails. It then reads: a pending ungotten character (and clears ch_have_ungotchar), or one byte of help data, or iread of the rest of the block. READ_INTR returns EOI; READ_AGAIN is treated as zero bytes; any other negative result shows 'read error' and is treated as zero bytes. With a log file configured the new data is written to it. On zero bytes it records ch_fsize (unless read-again), may show the waiting message and sleep 50 ms (ignore_eoi or read-again), returns EOI if follow-by-name sees the current file changed (after screen_trashed_num(2)), if sigs is set, or if it was reading a pipe at EOF; otherwise it loops. When data is available the buffer is moved to the head of the chains and the byte is returned.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): ch_have_ungotchar is cleared at line 274 when a pushed-back char is consumed (the slice 1-264 cut that part); old prose also wrongly listed a plain read error as returning EOI immediately; contract dropped (only bounded the result)

name: cmd_repaint
prose: public void cmd_repaint(constant char *old_cp) (less cmdbuf.c lines 280-318). Precondition: old_cp is NULL or points into cmdbuf at a character boundary at or after the current cp; cmd_col is the display column of cp. Postcondition: if old_cp is NULL it is set to the current cp and cmd_home() is called (cmd_home steps cp left writing backspaces while cmd_col > prompt_col, then sets cp to cmdbuf + cmd_offset). It then clears to the end of line, writes characters from cp (not from old_cp) while the next character's width keeps cmd_col + width below sc_width, then writes any following zero-width characters, advancing cp and cmd_col. Finally it calls cmd_left repeatedly while cp > old_cp (cmd_left may call cmd_rshift, which recursively repaints), so cp ends at or before old_cp (at the last character boundary reached). It returns nothing, does not modify cmdbuf, and changes cp, cmd_col, possibly cmd_offset, and the terminal contents.
note: reviewer-claim (round 1, repaints from cp not old_cp) is consistent with the code; prose restated to say it writes from the current cp

name: cmd_right
prose: static int cmd_right(void) (less cmdbuf.c lines 399-428). Precondition: cp points to a character boundary within cmdbuf and cmd_col is the display column of cp. Postcondition: returns CC_OK on both paths. If *cp is '\0' nothing changes. Otherwise it computes the next character (ncp, width, printable form pr) with cmd_step_right; if cmd_col + width >= sc_width, or cmd_col + width == sc_width - 1 and cp[1] != '\0', it first calls cmd_lshift(), which sets a new cmd_offset, homes the cursor and repaints the line so that cp again points at the same character, but cmd_col then holds the column of cp in the shifted display (not its old value). Then cp is set to ncp, cmd_col is increased by width, pr is written with putstr, and any directly following zero-width characters are written and skipped by advancing cp. cmdbuf contents are not modified.
note: old prose wrongly said cmd_lshift leaves cmd_col at its original value; cmd_lshift ends in cmd_home+cmd_repaint so cmd_col is recomputed for the shifted display (lines 333-365)

name: cmd_left
prose: static int cmd_left(void) (less cmdbuf.c lines 433-458). Precondition: cp points to a character boundary within cmdbuf and cmd_col is the display column of cp. Postcondition: returns CC_OK on both paths. If cp <= cmdbuf nothing changes. Otherwise it steps a copy ncp of cp left over characters until it passes one with non-zero width (stopping at cmdbuf), obtaining width and bswidth for the last character stepped over; if cmd_col < prompt_col + width it first calls cmd_rshift(), which changes cmd_offset, homes the cursor and repaints so that cp points at the same character, but cmd_col then holds the column of cp in the shifted display. Then cp is set to ncp, cmd_col is decreased by width, and bswidth backspaces are written. cmdbuf contents are not modified.
note: same correction as cmd_right: after cmd_rshift cmd_col is the column in the shifted display (lines 370-394)

name: cmd_edit
prose: static int cmd_edit(char c, lbool stay_in_completion) (less cmdbuf.c lines 843-963; returns CC_PASS, CC_OK or CC_QUIT). Precondition: the global command-buffer state is consistent. Postcondition: flags start at 0; with CMD_HISTORY and curr_mlist == NULL ECF_NOHISTORY is added; ECF_NOCOMPLETE is added unless completion is allowed (curr_mlist == NULL with CF_OPTION set in curr_cmdflags, or, with TAB_COMPLETE_FILENAME, curr_mlist is ml_examine or ml_shell). It maps c with editchar(c, flags); if is_ignoring_input(action) it returns CC_OK without touching in_completion. Otherwise by action: A_NOACTION returns CC_OK; EC_START_PASTE sets pasting = TRUE only when no_paste is set and returns CC_OK; EC_END_PASTE calls stop_ignoring_input() and returns CC_OK; EC_LITERAL sets literal = TRUE and returns CC_OK; EC_F_COMPLETE, EC_B_COMPLETE and EC_EXPAND return cmd_complete(action) and leave in_completion alone. All other handled actions first run not_in_completion (which sets in_completion = FALSE unless stay_in_completion is true): EC_RIGHT and EC_LEFT return cmd_right()/cmd_left(); EC_W_RIGHT moves right over non-space characters then over spaces and returns CC_OK; EC_W_LEFT moves left over spaces then non-spaces and returns CC_OK; EC_HOME sets cmd_offset = 0, calls cmd_home and cmd_repaint(cp), returns CC_OK; EC_END moves right to the end of the line, CC_OK; EC_INSERT toggles insert_mode only when LESS_INSERT_MODE is compiled in, returns CC_OK; EC_BACKSPACE, EC_LINEKILL, EC_W_BACKSPACE, EC_DELETE and EC_W_DELETE return the result of cmd_erase, cmd_kill, cmd_werase, cmd_delete and cmd_wdelete; EC_ABORT calls cmd_kill and returns CC_QUIT; with CMD_HISTORY, EC_UP and EC_DOWN return cmd_updown(action); any other action (including EC_UP/EC_DOWN when CMD_HISTORY is not compiled in) returns CC_PASS after not_in_completion.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): ECF_NOHISTORY, EC_UP/EC_DOWN and the ml_examine/ml_shell completion condition are conditional on CMD_HISTORY / TAB_COMPLETE_FILENAME; R2 (in_completion not cleared for some actions) was already covered

name: store_ansi
prose: static int store_ansi(LWCHAR ch, constant char *rep, POSITION pos) (less line.c lines 1195-1237). Precondition: line_ansi is non-NULL and holds the escape-sequence parse state of the line being built. Postcondition: it calls ansi_step2(line_ansi, ch, pos != NULL_POSITION) and acts on the result. ANSI_MID: STORE_CHAR(ch, AT_ANSI, rep, pos), where STORE_CHAR returns 1 from this function if store_char returns non-zero (store_char returns 1 when the character does not fit on the screen line); otherwise it sets hlink_in_line if the OSC-8 state is OSC_TYPENUM or OSC_STRING and appends ch to last_ansi. ANSI_END: the same STORE_CHAR (possible return 1), then ansi_done(line_ansi), line_ansi = NULL, ch appended to last_ansi, last_ansi copied into last_ansis[curr_last_ansi], last_ansi reset, and curr_last_ansi advanced modulo NUM_LAST_ANSIS (3). ANSI_ERR: removes the whole unrecognised sequence from the end of the buffer being written (shifted_ansi if cshift < hshift, otherwise linebuf), resets last_ansi, calls ansi_done and sets line_ansi = NULL. Any other result changes nothing. It returns 0 in every case except the STORE_CHAR early return of 1.
note: reviewers: R1 (STORE_CHAR can return 1) RIGHT, R2 (always 0) WRONG, R15 (ANSI_ERR may remove from shifted_ansi) RIGHT (lines 1220-1227, 841)

name: main
prose: int main(int argc, constant char *argv[]) of less (main.c lines 242-514). Postcondition: it initialises the program state (security, marks, commands, charset, line, history, options, search, prompt), treats the program name 'more' as less-is-more mode, scans the LESS or MORE environment options and then the command-line arguments (non-option arguments are collected as file names; '--' ends options; POSIXLY_CORRECT also ends options after the first file name). If a trailing option still wants a string argument it reports that with nopendopt() and calls quit(QUIT_OK). It then reads the terminal description, determines the editor settings (VISUAL, EDITOR, LESSEDIT) when EDITOR is compiled in, and registers the help file (when requested) and every file name with get_ifile. If stdout is not a terminal it copies each input file to the output via edit_first/cat_file/edit_next and calls quit(QUIT_OK). Otherwise it sets up the terminal and signals and selects the first file: with a -t tag option it quits with QUIT_ERROR if file names were also given, if edit_tagfile fails or if tagsearch finds no position; otherwise it quits with QUIT_ERROR if edit_first fails, and may check whether one screen is enough for -F. It applies a pending header option, waits for RETURN if error messages were shown, switches output to the terminal, runs commands() and calls quit(QUIT_OK). Every exit goes through quit(), so the final 'return 0' is not expected to be reached.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): a pending option without its string calls quit(QUIT_OK), not QUIT_ERROR (lines 343-351); slice cut head, real function is main at line 242

name: fs_walk
prose: static int fs_walk(void *softc, struct l9p_request *req) in lib9p/backend/fs.c (lines 1780-1976; the packet named it fs_twalk, but the function defined there is fs_walk). Precondition: req->lr_fid->lo_aux is a valid fs_fid (ff_name, ff_dirfd, ff_ai), req->lr_newfid is a valid fid (possibly the same as lr_fid), and req->lr_req.twalk.nwname (at most L9P_MAX_WELEM) names are in wname. Postcondition: it copies the base name into a MAXPATHLEN buffer and returns ENAMETOOLONG if it does not fit, or errno if fstatat of the base fails (no state changed, no ACL fetched yet). Then for each name i: if the current node is not a directory it jumps to cleanup with ENOTDIR; if check_access for execute fails it jumps to cleanup with EPERM (both returned even when earlier names succeeded); a name containing '/' or equal to '.' sets EINVAL and stops the loop; '..' at the root stops the loop with i reset to 0 and no error (success with nwqid 0); a combined path longer than MAXPATHLEN sets ENAMETOOLONG and stops; a failed fstatat of the next path sets ENOENT and stops; on success it fills rwalk.wqid[i] with the qid, swaps the name buffers and refetches the ACL with getacl(file, -1, next), freeing the previous separately allocated ACL. After the loop an error from a stopping name is returned only when i == 0 (no new fid stored, nwqid unset); if i > 0 the error is reset to 0 and the walk reports partial success. On success it opens the last good path with open_fid; if that returns NULL it returns ENOMEM (no new fid, nwqid unset). If lr_newfid == lr_fid the old fs_fid is freed with fs_freefid first. It stores the new fs_fid in lr_newfid->lo_aux, hands a separately allocated ACL to the new fs_fid when lr_newfid != lr_fid, sets rwalk.nwqid = i, and returns 0. On error paths a separately allocated ACL is freed, except that when lr_newfid == lr_fid and the new fid was installed, an ACL that was not the old fid's own is not freed or handed over (leaked).
note: slice cut head; real function name is fs_walk; read whole function including cleanup label
